grades.quote: These new mechanisms are not as well integrated with the Java programming language as the ones I described, but do have the feature of allowing multiple condition variables per mutex.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary information about associating condition variables with mutexes, but does not explain monitor operation.
Explains condition-variable waiting and demonstrates its combination with synchronized monitor methods and notification after state changes.

grades.quote: sleep() releases the condition lock so that the code calling wakeup() can proceed. sleep() also context-switches to the scheduler in order to let other threads run while it is waiting. The implementation performs these two steps in a way that is atomic (indivisible) with respect to wakeup(), to prevent lost wake-ups.
grades.reason: Explains the relevant lock-and-condition waiting mechanism, although not the monitor abstraction itself.
Contains only a page heading, with no explanation of synchronization.
